root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Pseudo-Tarrasch Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 c5 5. cxd5

overview: After 4.Bg5 c5 5.cxd5 White takes on d5 and Black recaptures with ...cxd4 and the Prins 6.Qxd4 Be7 7.e4 Nc6, or ...Qb6. White has a central pawn and development lead, while Black has piece play against the centre. The play is open and tactical.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with e4 and use the lead

black_ideas.idea: Hit the queen with ...Nc6 and recapture on d5

character.notes: The Prins and Canal lines (5.cxd5 cxd4 6.Qxd4 Be7 7.e4 Nc6) trade centre pawns early and leave tactical play against the king and the queen.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: A recognised line where Black equalises with accurate play.

structure.notes: The c- and d-pawns are traded, leaving a fluid centre and an open d-file.

approach.notes: A standard Pseudo-Tarrasch / Dutch-Peruvian line, played at strong level.

level.notes: Needs the main line sequences plus the resulting middlegames.

character.reason: Early exchanges and queen moves lead to tactical, forcing play.

gambit.reason: The pawn on d5 is recaptured at once.

structure.reason: Centre pawns come off and the pieces take the open lines.

level.reason: Concrete theory and active piece play.

plans.reason: White tries to use a lead in development.
